title: The four-chamber heart in motion
sub: A frontal cutaway driven by a pressure model. Every valve opens only when the pressure behind it beats the pressure ahead of it; watch the gradients, not the clock.
conditions: Frontal cutaway of all four chambers with both circulations

phases.name: Diastasis
phases.shows: Atrial and ventricular pressures nearly equal; slow filling straight from the veins.

phases.name: Atrial systole
phases.shows: The atria contract (a wave) and top up the ventricles; atrioventricular valves open, semilunar valves shut.

phases.name: Isovolumetric contraction
phases.shows: Ventricles contract with all four valves shut (S1 at AV closure); pressure rises steeply at constant volume.

phases.name: Ventricular ejection
phases.shows: LV pressure exceeds aortic (~80 mmHg) and RV exceeds pulmonary pressure; semilunar valves open and the stroke volume is ejected; LV peaks near 120 mmHg.

phases.name: Isovolumetric relaxation
phases.shows: Ventricles relax with all valves shut; aortic valve closure gives S2 and the dicrotic notch; pressure falls at constant volume (ESV).

phases.name: Rapid filling
phases.shows: Ventricular pressure falls below atrial; AV valves open and most ventricular filling occurs passively.

parts.name: Right atrium
parts.shows: Right atrium: receives deoxygenated blood from the venae cavae; contracts in atrial systole.

parts.name: Right ventricle
parts.shows: Right ventricle: pumps into the pulmonary artery at low pressure (~20 mmHg systolic).

parts.name: Left atrium
parts.shows: Left atrium: receives oxygenated blood from the pulmonary veins; pressure ~5–10 mmHg.

parts.name: Left ventricle
parts.shows: Left ventricle: thick-walled pump into the aorta; pressure 0–120 mmHg, volume ~125 → ~55 mL.

parts.name: Tricuspid valve
parts.shows: Tricuspid valve: right atrioventricular valve; opens when RA pressure > RV pressure.

parts.name: Pulmonary valve
parts.shows: Pulmonary valve: right semilunar valve; opens when RV pressure > pulmonary artery pressure.

parts.name: Mitral valve
parts.shows: Mitral valve: left atrioventricular valve; opens when LA pressure > LV pressure; its closure contributes to S1.

parts.name: Aortic valve
parts.shows: Aortic valve: left semilunar valve; opens when LV pressure > aortic pressure; its closure contributes to S2.

parts.name: Aorta
parts.shows: Aorta: receives the LV stroke volume; elastic recoil keeps diastolic pressure ~80 mmHg.

parts.name: Pulmonary artery
parts.shows: Pulmonary trunk and arteries: carry RV output to the lungs.

parts.name: Venae cavae
parts.shows: Superior and inferior venae cavae: return systemic venous blood to the right atrium.

parts.name: Pulmonary veins
parts.shows: Pulmonary veins: return oxygenated blood to the left atrium.

readouts.label: LA pressure
readouts.shows: Left atrial pressure (a, c and v waves).

readouts.label: RA pressure
readouts.shows: Right atrial pressure (≈ central venous pressure).

readouts.label: ECG
readouts.shows: Schematic surface ECG on the same clock: P wave starts atrial contraction, QRS just before ventricular contraction, T wave during late ejection.

readouts.label: LV volume
readouts.shows: Left ventricular volume: end-diastolic volume at its peak, end-systolic volume at its trough.

readouts.label: Stroke vol · EF
readouts.shows: Stroke volume = end-diastolic minus end-systolic volume.

readouts.label: Ejection fraction
readouts.shows: Ejection fraction = stroke volume / end-diastolic volume.

concepts: Wiggers diagram: pressure and volume against time
pressure gradients open and close the valves
first heart sound (S1) and second heart sound (S2)
end-diastolic volume, end-systolic volume, stroke volume, ejection fraction
aortic pressure: systolic, diastolic, dicrotic notch
pulmonary and systemic circulations through the four chambers
not_shown: ECG waves (P, QRS, T) as a trace
Frank–Starling mechanism / changing preload or afterload
effect of heart rate on the cycle
